summary: Canada. Federal parliamentary democracy (parliament of canada) under a constitutional monarchy; a commonwealth realm; federal and state authorities and responsibilities regulated in constitution.
rulers: King CHARLES III (since 8 September 2022); represented by Governor General Mary SIMON (since 26 July 2021); Prime Minister Mark CARNEY (since 14 March 2025)
government: federal parliamentary democracy (Parliament of Canada) under a constitutional monarchy; a Commonwealth realm; federal and state authorities and responsibilities regulated in constitution
economy: high-income economy and second-largest US trading partner; key timber, oil, and gas industries; trade uncertainties and weak business investments contributing to economic slowdown; high and growing public debt; inflation moderating but remains above target range GDP (PPP): $2.341 trillion (2024 est.). note: data in 2021 dollars
military: Canadian Forces: Canadian Army, Royal Canadian Navy, Royal Canadian Air Force (2025) Expenditure: 2% of GDP (2025 est.)
origin: 1 July 1867 (union of British North American colonies); 11 December 1931 (recognized by UK per Statute of Westminster)

sourceFields.military: Canadian Forces: Canadian Army, Royal Canadian Navy, Royal Canadian Air Force (2025)
sourceFields.militaryNotes: note 1: the CAF is comprised of both a Regular Force and a Reserve Force; the Reserve Force is comprised of the Primary Reserve, Canadian Rangers, Cadet Organizations Administration and Training Service, and the Supplementary Reserve; the Canadian Rangers are part of the Army Reserve Force and provide a limited presence in Canada's northern, coastal, and isolated areas for sovereignty, public safety, and surveillance roles note 2: the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP or "Mounties") are under the Department of Public Safety; the Coast Guard is under the Department of Fisheries and Oceans
